_doc: Human-in-the-loop judgement overrides (ground rule: distorted data is handled per ticker, never by changing the general formula). Committed to git so they survive sandbox wipes; DB overrides (API PUT /override) layer on top. Keys: method, growth (yrs 1-5), growth_6_10, biz_type, iv_override, discount_rate, base_cf.

TMO.note: Consensus temporarily distorted very low after the post-COVID normalisation; Adam kept the prior long-term rate (heavenly-queen compounder). Use ~13% long-run EPS growth (pre-distortion consensus band 12-15%). Force DCF on FCF (Adam's method for TMO) instead of the P/S fallback the selector picks when the distorted data breaks consistency.

ASML.note: 5y EPS estimates (FinViz 42%, Zacks 52%) look like a cyclical rebound off a depressed base and hit the 40% cap; next-year estimates are ~34-38%. Normalised to 20% (judgement; revisit when consensus settles).

AVGO.note: FinViz 5y EPS 65% (next-year ~62-67%) reflects the current AI ramp; not plausible as a 5-year average at this scale. Normalised to 25% (judgement).

BABA.note: FinViz 43% is a rebound off depressed earnings (regulatory crackdown base). Zacks long-term 13% used.

VEEV.note: Sources disagree wildly (FinViz 12.5%, Zacks 35%); next-year estimates ~10-20%. Use 18% (judgement, between sources).

PLTR.note: Now consistently FCF-positive with rising FCF; Adam values it on DCF rather than PSG. Speculative sizing still applies.

ACGL.note: Specialty (re)insurer: book value compounding is the value driver; Adam's IV (109.38) matches P/B valuation (108.4). DNI overstates because float-driven earnings are lumpy.
